chunks: And Mismāʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Baṣrī narrated from him that he said:
“There is no issue in taking from the silk covering of the Kaʿbah and making it a cover for a muṣḥaf, or making it a prayer-place upon which one prays.”

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Kaʿbah, the sacred sanctuary in Makkah
key_terms.دِيبَاجِ: silk brocade or fine silk fabric
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem or prohibition
key_terms.مُصَلًّى: a place or mat for performing salat
key_terms.مُصْحَفٍ: a written copy of the Qur'an

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use cloth from the covering of the Kaʿbah as a muṣḥaf cover or prayer mat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling permitting the use of fabric from the covering of the Kaʿbah for respectful devotional purposes. It specifically allows making it into a cover for a muṣḥaf or a prayer mat used for salat.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.813 - It was narrated from Mus'ab ibn Abdul Malik al-Basri that He said:
"There is no issue in taking (a piece) from the silk covering of the Ka’ba and using it as a cover for a Quran or making it into a prayer mat to pray upon."
